stem: A Massachusetts collaborating pharmacist wants an appropriately trained certified technician to collect the vital signs contemplated by her collaborative practice agreement. The agreement says nothing at all about delegation. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Silence in the agreement operates as permission to delegate the duty.
Delegation is permitted because the technician is appropriately trained.
Delegation is permitted because collecting vital signs is not a dispensing act.
The agreement must specify which of the pharmacist's duties may be delegated.
The agreement must specify which duties under it may not be delegated.

explanation.core_reasoning: 247 CMR 16.04(3) requires a collaborative practice agreement to specify those duties of the authorized pharmacist that MAY be delegated to other appropriately trained and authorized staff AND those duties under the agreement that SHALL NOT be delegated. An agreement that says nothing has not met either requirement, so there is no delegation power to exercise.

choice_analysis.A: The regulation requires affirmative specification, so silence is not permission.
choice_analysis.B: Training is necessary but does not supply the missing agreement terms.
choice_analysis.C: The nature of the task does not remove the requirement to specify.
choice_analysis.D: Correct: the delegable duties must be named.
choice_analysis.E: Correct: the non-delegable duties must also be named.

related_facts: Intern and technician support must still comply with 247 CMR 8.01 and 8.02 through 8.06
explanation.mpje_trap: Candidates reason from the competence of the staff member rather than from the content of the agreement.

reasoning_steps: Ask what the agreement must contain before any delegation is possible
Note that both the delegable and the non-delegable duties must be specified
Conclude that an agreement silent on delegation confers no delegation power
